name: Superphosphate fertiliser, Rothamsted and Deptford, England
summary: Bones or mineral phosphates treated with sulphuric acid to make superphosphate, a fertiliser patented by John Bennet Lawes in 1842 and made in his Deptford factory from 1843.
description: John Bennet Lawes patented in 1842 a process for making a fertiliser, superphosphate, by treating bones or mineral phosphates with sulphuric acid. His first factory, at Deptford Creek, opened in 1843; raw materials including sulphuric acid came in by boat and 'J. B. Lawes's Patent Manures' were shipped out.

impact.note: Factory superphosphate spread through farming in many countries (reach 2, not 3: no source here measures a share of humanity, so the lower score is taken), made bought mineral nutrients a new means of keeping land fertile (depth 2), and began the manufactured-fertiliser industry (generativity 2).

date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: Lawes's process for making superphosphate fertiliser by treating bones or mineral phosphates with sulphuric acid was granted patent No. 9353 in 1842; Rothamsted's history gives the month as November.

evidence.supports: Lawes' process for manufacturing superphosphate fertiliser, by treating bones or mineral phosphates with sulphuric acid, was granted a patent (No. 9353) in November 1842.

date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: Lawes's first factory for superphosphate was opened at Deptford Creek in 1843.

evidence.supports: Lawes' first factory, which was at Deptford Creek, was opened in 1843.
evidence.locator: Timeline entry for 1843, "Establishment of Lawes Manure Company"

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: James Murray's priority: his Dublin work on soluble phosphate (his Advice to Farmers, 1841), the English and Scottish patents his son took out, and the later sale of his patent (the Irish Times column does not name the buyer, usually said to be Lawes) were not checked against a primary source. Cooper and Davis, The Irish Fertiliser Industry: A History (2004), should be consulted, and Liebig's 1840 proposal to treat bones with acid compared.

The month of Lawes's patent: Rothamsted gives November 1842, while other accounts date the patent 23 May 1842 (November may be the enrolment of the specification). The event is therefore dated to the year only.
The guano and nitrate trades from Peru and Chile, which ran alongside superphosphate, need their own research.

research.note: Rothamsted's history records Lawes's 1842 patent and 1843 factory but does not call either the first, and an Irish Times column says James Murray's fertiliser-manufacture patent was bought by a later industrialist (unnamed there) who 'got the credit for the discovery of superphosphates, though Murray deserved it'; neither priority nor independence was established from a checked source, so the origin is left unknown.
